themes.title: Section 338 Canada tariffs — Aug 21 EOD binary resolving: LeBlanc/Greer announced deal Aug 19, documentation still being finalized, tariff effective Aug 22 12:01am ET if not formally revoked
themes.summary: As of August 21, the Section 338 binary is in its final hours of resolution. Per Policy Magazine (Aug 20), Canadian Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc and USTR Jamieson Greer announced on August 19 that 'a trade deal has been struck between the two countries to break the deadlock over the future of CUSMA.' Prime Minister Carney's congratulatory post referred to 'significant progress,' a deliberately softer formulation than a signed agreement — a signal that documentation and details remain outstanding. The operative hard deadline for CBP and FX markets remains August 22 at 12:01am ET: per GHY International, a shipment that leaves Canada on August 21 but is entered for consumption after midnight August 22 attracts the 50% levy regardless of deal language. The three-day pause announced hours before the August 19 12:01am ET deadline was Trump's mechanism to allow negotiators to 'finish the documentation' per Policy Magazine. The framework under negotiation involves five key tests per Policy Magazine: (1) autos resolution; (2) steel and aluminum terms; (3) what Canada concedes on dairy, alcohol and retaliatory tariffs; (4) the meaning of 'economic security' and 'digital trade alignment'; (5) whether CUSMA's long-term credibility is restored. Canadian premiers conditioned the alcohol-ban removal on meaningful Section 232 tariff rollbacks. Quebec Premier Frechette's red line on dairy supply management remains the most politically sensitive unresolved point. The statutory mechanics are unchanged: 50% additional ad valorem tariff on approximately $20 billion of Canadian goods (motor vehicles, dairy, alcoholic beverages, cement, furniture, clothing, and others), stacking on all existing duties with no USMCA/CUSMA exemption. Energy, potash, fish, critical minerals, and Section 232-covered goods remain excluded. Three scenarios are live entering the Aug 21 close: (1) Deal proclamation formally signed and published by Aug 21 EOD — now the highest-probability path given LeBlanc/Greer announcement and Trump's prior 'very good deal' framing; (2) Further extension while documentation is finalised — moderate probability if legal/political sticking points slow signing; (3) Tariffs land Aug 22 — tail risk but non-trivial given Carney's 'significant progress' language (not 'deal signed') and unresolved provincial supply-management red lines.

implications.CAD: Deal announcement partially priced on Aug 19-20 open — USDCAD should have compressed toward 1.3850-1.3900 range. Final Aug 21 resolution dominates: (1) Formal deal proclamation by Aug 21 EOD = sharp CAD relief rally, 100-150 pips from pre-Aug 19 levels, theme retires upon formal revocation of Section 338 proclamations — this is now the base case given LeBlanc/Greer public announcement; (2) Further extension = 30-50 pip CAD relief, theme extends with reduced anxiety premium; (3) Tariffs land Aug 22 = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips, Canada retaliation cliff materialises. The deal's long-term CAD implications depend critically on whether Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs are meaningfully reduced — a shallow deal leaves structural CAD headwinds in place.
implications.USD: USDCAD directional narrative dominated by Aug 21 binary. Broad USD softness from data miss trifecta and Jackson Hole positioning is secondary counterweight. Post-Aug 21 resolution (either direction), Fed/Jackson Hole theme reasserts as the primary USD driver.
implications.MXN: Secondary exposure — USDMXN may telegraph risk sentiment around Canada shock. US-Mexico USMCA track advancing more smoothly per prior reporting.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD may be volatile around Aug 21 resolution. EU under separate tariff ceiling; EU-Canada trade linkage adds modest contagion risk to EUR crosses in a CAD shock scenario.
implications.AUD: Indirect risk-off commodity bloc contagion if CAD volatility spills broadly on Aug 21. AUDCAD may spike on the binary outcome.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol spike risk around Aug 21 close.

themes.title: Japan-US joint FX intervention regime — Japan national CPI Aug 21 in-line at 1.9%/1.8% core, USDJPY flatlines near 159, BOJ Sep hike ~80% priced, Sep 17-18 is the live hard binary
themes.summary: As of August 21, Japan's national CPI for July has been released and represents the most significant near-term data catalyst for the BOJ. The headline CPI rose 1.9% YoY (Japan Times/CNBC) and the core reading excluding fresh food came in at 1.8% YoY — the fastest pace since January, matching the median economist estimate and picking up from 1.6% in the prior month per Bloomberg. The BOJ-watched measure stripping out both fresh food and energy advanced 1.9% YoY per Japan Times. Critically, per FXStreet, the national headline CPI including all items rose to 2.0% YoY in July from 1.6% in June (revised from the prior 1.7% reading). USDJPY flatlined near 158.96-159.05 in the early Asian session on the print — the in-line result carried insufficient surprise to catalyse a breakout, with growing BOJ hike speculation offsetting the GDP weakness noted earlier this week. State Street's APAC economist Krishna Bhimavarapu stated the rise in headline inflation to 1.9% 'strengthens our conviction that the BOJ's next move is likely to be a rate hike in September.' The BOJ September hike case remains ~80% priced per MUFG. The intervention regime remains in a consolidation phase — no follow-up intervention has landed since the initial joint US-Japan action in late July/early August (approximate low of ~155.20 on August 3), a gap of over two and a half weeks allowing carry traders to rebuild short-JPY positions. USDJPY at 158.96-159.05 sits roughly 3% below the 2026 high of 163.85 set on July 28. The BOJ's July meeting (8-1, Takata dissented for immediate hike to 1.25%) kept rates at 1.0% and warned underlying inflation could exceed 2%. BOJ June meeting minutes (released August 10) showed most board members judged crude oil costs were filtering through to consumer prices broadly, with several warning underlying inflation could overshoot 2%. The BOJ warned in its outlook report that core inflation was likely to accelerate to a level 'clearly above' 2% from the second half of its fiscal 2026 (September-March). Reuters, citing three sources familiar with BOJ thinking, reports the BOJ is set to raise rates as soon as September and likely to hike more aggressively thereafter. MUFG projects BOJ to raise to 1.25% in September 2026, 1.50% in January 2027, and 1.75% in June 2027. Structural backdrop unchanged: BOJ at 1.0% vs Fed at 3.50-3.75%, wide but narrowing rate differential; JGB 10-year at 30-year highs; yen short positioning still elevated. Next hard catalyst: BOJ Sep 17-18 meeting.

implications.JPY: MAXIMUM tailwind from three converging forces: (1) G2 intervention with Bessent re-entry warning nominally active; (2) BOJ Sep hike ~80% priced, cemented by in-line CPI; (3) Fed Sep hike odds volatile around 31-40%, narrowing rate differential from both sides. Counter-risk: USDJPY at 158.96-159.05 with no follow-up intervention for 18+ days allows carry rebuild. If 160 breaks on a daily close without official response, regime credibility damage will be severe. CPI print came in-line — no material JPY reaction on the day; Sep hike remains the dominant forward catalyst.
implications.USD: BOJ intervention chatter and growing hike pricing actively depressing rate-differential support for USDJPY. USDJPY topside capped by intervention threat and ~80% Sep BOJ hike pricing. Hawkish FOMC minutes (Aug 19) provide modest USD support but Jackson Hole Aug 28 dominates the USD narrative from here.

implications.CAD: CADJPY lower; CAD FX dominated by Section 338 binary Aug 21 above all else.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention pressure. Watch AUDJPY 93-95 range. AUDUSD on multi-week winning streak.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY 160.00 is the immediate critical level — a daily close above 160 without official verbal or actual intervention signals carry traders overpowering the regime and constitutes a credibility break. USDJPY below 157.50 = intervention credibility reasserting. USDJPY below 155.20 (post-intervention low Aug 3) = regime decisively winning. Japan national CPI Aug 21 RELEASED: headline 2.0% YoY / core 1.8% YoY — in-line, confirms Sep BOJ hike trajectory, no material USDJPY reaction. BOJ Sep 17-18 meeting is the live hard binary: hike to 1.25% = fundamental JPY support materialises, reduces intervention burden; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 160+ re-test. Jackson Hole Aug 28 (Warsh keynote) — dovish USD framing extends JPY-positive environment; hawkish framing partially restores rate differential drag on JPY. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately. JGB 10-year at 30-year highs — if approaches 3.0%, BOJ forced to defend bonds vs yen simultaneously.

themes.title: Warsh Fed — FOMC minutes Aug 19 hawkish (many members see further hikes if inflation persists), Sep hike odds 31-40%, Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 is dominant USD binary (Warsh keynote Aug 28), July PCE Aug 27 pre-keynote risk
themes.summary: As of August 21, the FOMC minutes from the July 28-29 meeting (released August 19 at 2:00pm ET) delivered a hawkish read. Per Brisk Markets, 'many Federal Reserve policymakers believe further interest-rate increases could become necessary if inflation fails to moderate,' and crucially the hawkish sentiment extended beyond the three formal dissenters. The three voting dissenters were confirmed as regional Fed presidents Logan, Hammack, and Kashkari — the first unified three-way dissent since September 2016 per Pip Theory. Newsquawk's preview highlighted that the key variable was how far hawkish sentiment extended beyond the dissenters — whether 'many' or 'several' members expressed sympathy — as that distinction is what September pricing hinges on. Per ING (pre-release), they conceded 'there may be a few hawkish references in tonight's minutes that could nudge the Dollar and short-dated rates a little firmer' while arguing the minutes were unlikely to be a game changer. DXY was trading near 99.38-99.50 ahead of and at the time of the minutes release. EUR/USD entered the week near 1.1590 (2-month high since mid-June). GBP/USD near 1.3560 (3-month highs), with additional GBP-specific support from UK July CPI at 2.9% YoY (above prior 2.6%, per FXStreet). September hike odds have been volatile in the 31-40% range — Pip Theory marked odds at ~31% ahead of the minutes (down from ~two-thirds at the July meeting), Newsquawk's preview had them at ~35%, and the prior summary had ~39-40%. The hawkish minutes will put upward pressure on Sep hike pricing, but the dominant forward event is now Jackson Hole. The symposium runs August 27-29 under the theme 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy,' with roughly 120 central bankers from over 70 countries attending. Kevin Warsh delivers his first keynote as Fed Chair on Friday morning, August 28 — his first Jackson Hole address since taking office on May 22, 2026, 19 days before the September 16 FOMC decision. Under Warsh, the Fed no longer telegraphs intentions ahead of meetings, and he has curtailed forward guidance and shortened the post-meeting statement per Investinglive. Warsh told reporters July 29 the speech will 'frame the big questions' and he is 'not constrained by market prices,' while noting the constant cycle creates a tendency to 'get caught up in the myopic.' Half the FOMC pencilled in 2026 hikes at June meeting; three presidents dissented for hikes in July. July PCE releases August 27 (the opening morning of Jackson Hole) — creating a potential data/event cascade with Nvidia earnings August 26 evening 36 hours ahead. Sep 11 CPI (August data) is the next major data event post-JH. Sep 16 FOMC is the hard policy event.
